UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                 BEFORE THE
                   FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION




Northern Indiana Public Service              )
Company LLC                                  )
                                             )
v.                                           )              Docket No. EL26-36-000
                                             )

      Operator, Inc.                         )


              LIMITED COMMENTS OF THE SOUTHERN REGULATORS

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”

or “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214, and the

Combined Notice #1 issued on December 31, 2025, the Arkansas Public Service Commission and

the Council of the City of New Orleans (collectively "Southern Regulators"), 1 submit these limited

comments to the Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC’s (“NIPSCO”) “Complaint and

Request for Fast Track Processing,” filed on December 29, 2025. 2

       As detailed below, the instant Complaint is fact specific.        Therefore, the Southern

Regulators request that any Commission findings or directives in this proceeding also be limited

to the facts in the Complaint.




1
       Each of the Southern Regulators have filed their own doc-less interventions in this docket,
       and therefore, are already parties to this proceeding.
2
       See N. Ind. Pub. Serv. Co. LLC v. Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., Docket No.
       EL26-36-000 (Dec. 29, 2025) (“Complaint”).

                                                 -1-
 I.     BACKGROUND

       R.M. Schahfer Generating Station is an electric generating facility located in Posey County,

Indiana. The Schahfer facility is owned and operated by NIPSCO and consists of two coal-fired

generation units, Unit 17 (345 MW) and Unit 18 (345 MW), with a combined nameplate capacity

of approximately 690 MW. Unit 17 and Unit 18 began commercial operations in the mid-1980s.

Both units have been subject to long-term retirement planning and were scheduled for retirement

on December 31, 2025, consistent with NIPSCO’s commitments in the Indiana Utility Regulatory

Commission approved settlement agreements in Cause Nos. 45772 (August 2, 2023) and 46120

(June 26, 2025).3

       On December 23, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of Energy issued an order pursuant to Federal

Power Act (“FPA”) section 202(c) and section 301(b) of the Department of Energy Organization

Act4 declaring that “an emergency exists in portions of the Midwest region of the United States

due to a shortage of electric energy, a shortage of facilities for the generation of electric energy,

and other causes.”5 Accordingly, the DOE Order directed that both NIPSCO and Midcontinent

Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) “take all measures necessary to ensure” that the

Schahfer Units 17 and 18 are available to operate until March 23, 2026. 6

       In complying with the DOE Order, NIPSCO is incurring and will continue to incur costs

as it makes the Schahfer Units available into the MISO market and produces energy when

dispatched.   However, MISO’s existing Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating

associated with complying with the DOE Order.7 In addition, MISO lacks Tariff authority to

unilaterally offer NIPSCO a FPA section 202(c) rate agreement. 8

       The DOE Order stated that “[r]ate recovery is available pursuant to [FPA section 202(c)],”

and further directed NIPSCO to “file with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Tariff

revisions or waivers necessary to effectuate this order.” 9 NIPSCO states that it intends to

separately file the actual costs associated with running the Schahfer Units 17 and 18 from the date

of the DOE Order, netting out applicable market revenues, i.e., its “Order Costs”.10 But, here,

NIPSCO files the instant Complaint requesting that the Commission exercise its authority pursuant

to FPA sections 202(c) and 309, or in the alternative section 206, to order MISO to adopt a Tariff

revision for NIPSCO to recover the Order Costs from complying with the DOE Order. 11 NIPSCO

requests that the requested MISO Tariff revision be effective as of the issuance of the DOE Order

on December 23, 2025, or such other date as the Commission finds appropriate to allow NIPSCO

to recover costs associated with the DOE 202(c) Order. 12

 II.    LIMITED COMMENTS

       Since 2020, the Department of Energy (“DOE”) has exercised its authority under Section

202(c) primarily in response to extreme weather conditions.13 In contrast, here the DOE has

declared emergency conditions exists under more generalized reliability concerns due to

“increasing demand and shortage from accelerated retirement of generation facilities…in the near

term and … likely to continue in subsequent years” 14 As a result, the DOE has taken the

extraordinary step of delaying the Schahfer Units 17 and 18’s planned retirement, requiring

NIPSCO to ensure the Schahfer Units are available to operate, and directing MISO to economically

dispatch the Schahfer Units “to minimize cost to ratepayers.” 15

       Due to the unique circumstances underlying the DOE Order and the relief requested under

the Complaint, the Southern Regulators submit these limited comments to ensure that the

Commission’s actions are confined to the specific facts presented in the Complaint.

       A.      NIPSCO’s Proposed Rate Recovery Mechanism is Applicable Only to the
               Schahfer Units 17 and 18.

       In the Complaint, NIPSCO’s only request for relief is for the Commission to direct MISO

to revise its Tariff to include a mechanism to effectuate NIPSCO’s cost recovery of the Order Costs

incurred due to the DOE Order.16 Specifically, Attachment B of the Complaint includes a proposed

 schedule for MISO’s Tariff entitled “Allocation of Costs Associated with Continued Availability

of NIPSCO’s Schahfer Units 17 and 18 Pursuant to DOE Order No. 202-25-12.” 17

       The Southern Regulators do not take a position on either NIPSCO’s requested relief, the

Commission’s authority to grant the requested relief, or whether NIPSCO’s proposed schedule is

just and reasonable. Rather, the Southern Regulators draw attention to the fact that both the DOE

Order and the proposed schedule contain explicit language that the cost recovery mechanism is

related only to the facts underlying the DOE Order and the Schahfer Units 17 and 18. In other

words, any rate recovery schedule that the Commission may accept in this proceeding will not be

of general applicability under MISO’s Tariff but will be limited to NIPSCO’s Schahfer Units 17

and 18 and the Order Costs incurred due to the DOE Order. The Southern Regulators request that

this point is made clear in any Commission order in this case.

       B.      As proposed, the Order Costs for the Schahfer Units 17 and 18 Are Not (and
               Should Not Be) Allocated to the MISO South Subregion.

       In addition to proposing a cost recovery mechanism for the Order Costs, the Complaint

also asks the Commission to adopt the cost allocation in its proposed schedule in Attachment B to

the Complaint.18 Specifically, NIPSCO proposes to allocate the Order Costs to MISO’s north and

central zones (i.e., Zones 1-7) on a load ratio share basis.19 In support, NIPSCO argues that the

DOE Order identified the reliability risks in those MISO zones as the basis for declaring the

emergency and requiring the continued operation of the Schahfer Units 17 and 18.20 Therefore,

 consistent with general beneficiary pays and cost causation principles, NIPSCO argues the

Commission should find its proposed cost allocation in Attachment B is just and reasonable. 21

       Again, the Southern Regulators do not take a position on either NIPSCO’s proposed cost

allocation to MISO Zones 1-7, the Commission’s authority to grant the requested cost allocation,

or whether NIPSCO demonstrated that such allocation is either appropriate or justified under cost

causation or beneficiary pays principles. But, the Southern Regulators agree that none of the Order

Costs should be allocated to the MISO South subregion. In doing so, the Southern Regulators do

not endorse the proposed scope of the cost allocation as defined by the DOE Order. Moreover,

due to the fact-specific Complaint, the Southern Regulators urge the Commission to make clear

that any finding or directive on cost allocation in this proceeding does not set any precedent for

future orders, pursuant to section 202(c).

 III.   CONCLUSION

       For the reasons stated above, the Southern Regulators respectfully request that the

Commission accept the limited comments submitted herein in conjunction with its determinations

on the Complaint in the instant proceeding.
